title: DA vs MDA (and the 91.175 Big Three)
hook: One altitude you decide AT. One you park ON. Mix them up and the FAA writes.

scenes.narration: Destination's got two approaches, kid: the I L S with minimums of two-eighty, and the V O R with minimums of six-forty. Same runway, same clouds — but the way you fly those two numbers is completely different.
The V O R approach, descending to six-forty with nothing in sight. Do you level off there, or keep descending while you decide? Commit.
Level off. M D A is a hard floor — ride it to the missed point, no sagging down to hunt for the airport.

The I L S is different. D A comes with a glidepath — keep descending, and AT two-eighty you decide: land or miss. Why is dipping a hair below built in? Momentum. The miss starts AT the number, and the procedure designers accounted for the arc.
Going below EITHER number takes all three: position for a normal landing, the required flight visibility, and the runway environment in sight. Two out of three is a missed approach with extra steps.
Eyes off the screen. D A or M D A — which one do you ride level, and what are the big three? Out loud.
D A: decide, in motion. M D A: level floor. Three conditions unlock the descent. My examiner in eighty-seven asked all of this — I still remember his frown.
From the I L S lesson — those standard minimums, one more time. Two numbers. Go.
Ninety-one one seventy-five, paragraph c. The whole ballgame.

quiz.question: Descending on the VOR approach, you reach MDA 640 with nothing in sight. You:
choices: Level off and maintain it until landing criteria or the missed point
Descend 100 ft lower to look for the runway
quiz.explanation: MDA is a floor you hold on a non-precision approach; DA is where you decide during a continuous guided descent.

quiz.question: Descending below DA or MDA requires (14 CFR 91.175(c)):
choices: Normal-landing position + required flight visibility + runway environment in sight
quiz.explanation: All three: continuous position for a normal descent/landing, the flight visibility on the plate, and a visual reference from the 91.175(c)(3) list.

quiz.question: Seeing ONLY the approach light system, you may descend below mins but no lower than:
choices: 100 ft above touchdown zone elevation (unless red terminating/side-row bars are visible)
You may not descend at all
quiz.explanation: 91.175(c)(3)(i): approach lights alone get you to 100 ft above TDZE — lower requires the red terminating or side-row bars, or another runway reference.
